evidence.quote: John Jones Pettus was born on October 9 , 1813 in Wilson County , Tennessee

events.text: Represented Kemper County in the Mississippi House of Representatives.

evidence.quote: In 1844 , Pettus represented Kemper County in the Mississippi House of Representatives .
In 1848 , he was elected to the Mississippi Senate .

events.text: Began service as acting governor after Foote's resignation.

evidence.quote: served as acting governor from January 5 to 10 , 1854

events.text: Ended acting governorship when McRae was sworn in.

evidence.quote: He held the governorship until McRae was sworn in on January 10 , 1854

events.text: Returned as president of the Mississippi Senate.

evidence.quote: On January 11 , McRae was inaugurated as Governor and Pettus returned as senate president

events.text: Began term as 23rd Governor of Mississippi after election.

evidence.quote: served as the 23rd Governor of Mississippi , from 1859 to 1863

events.text: Called special legislative session urging a secession convention.

evidence.quote: on November 26 , 1860 , Pettus called for a Special Session of the Legislature
Pettus was re-elected in the fall of 1861 .

events.text: Ended term as governor; succeeded by Charles Clark.

events.label: oath of allegiance
events.text: Took oath of allegiance to the United States government.

evidence.quote: In September 1865 he took the oath of allegiance to the United States government
Pettus died on January 25 , 1867 , of pneumonia

undated_mentions: opened law practice in Scooba, Mississippi (1840s)
educated at home by his mother (childhood)
served as president of the Mississippi Senate (before 1854)
ordered special session in Noxubee County to fill deceased representative's seat (during acting governorship, 1854)
commissioned colonel in state militia (after term limit)
failed three times to receive presidential pardon (after September 1865)
relocated to Pulaski County (present-day Lonoke County), Arkansas (after the war)
